subject: maths
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF

topics.title: Faces, edges and corners of 3D shapes
outcomes: Learner can count faces, edges and corners of cubes and cuboids
misconceptions: Counts only the faces that can be seen in a picture
hooks: A carrom striker box vs a dice

topics.title: Right angles and circles
outcomes: Learner can find right angles in objects and draw circles using a string or bangle
misconceptions: Thinks an angle is bigger if its arms are drawn longer
hooks: Corners of a book are right angles; is a clock’s 3 o’clock a right angle?

topics.title: Shapes on a grid
outcomes: Learner can draw and copy shapes on a square or dot grid
misconceptions: Thinks a shape on a grid changes when it is turned
hooks: Make a tile design for the courtyard

topics.title: Top, front and side views
outcomes: Learner can match objects to their top, front and side views
misconceptions: Believes the top view of a cylinder is a rectangle
hooks: View a glass, a cone and a box from above

topics.title: Reading simple grids and maps
outcomes: Learner can describe paths and positions on a simple grid map
misconceptions: Confuses left and right on a map when facing a different direction
hooks: Find hiding places in a playground map

topics.title: Odd and even numbers
outcomes: Learner can sort numbers as odd or even by pairing and predict odd + odd
misconceptions: Thinks a number is odd if it has any odd digit (e.g. 34 is odd)
hooks: Pair up students for a dance: is anyone left out?

topics.title: Number patterns
outcomes: Learner can continue and explain number and shape patterns
misconceptions: Believes a pattern can only increase
hooks: Patterns on a calendar page

topics.title: Numbers up to 9999
outcomes: Learner can read, write and represent 4-digit numbers with thousands, hundreds, tens and ones
misconceptions: Writes four thousand fifty as 40050 or 450
hooks: Spectators at a kabaddi match; price of a cycle

topics.title: Comparing and ordering 4-digit numbers
outcomes: Learner can compare and order 4-digit numbers and place them on a number line
misconceptions: Compares numbers digit by digit from the right
hooks: Which hill station is higher above sea level?

topics.title: Nearest hundred and thousand
outcomes: Learner can round numbers to the nearest 10, 100 or 1000 for estimating
misconceptions: Rounds 1450 to 2000 because 4 rounds up to 5
hooks: About how many people live in your village?

topics.title: Fractions as equal shares
outcomes: Learner can represent halves, thirds, quarters and similar fractions of shapes and collections
misconceptions: Believes 1/3 is bigger than 1/2 because 3 is bigger than 2
Thinks the parts need not be equal to be called thirds
hooks: Cutting a birthday cake or a watermelon fairly

topics.title: Fractions in measurement
outcomes: Learner can use fractions to describe lengths and quantities like half a kilo, three-quarter litre
misconceptions: Thinks 3/4 means 3 pieces regardless of size
hooks: Adha kilo tamatar, paav kilo dhaniya

topics.title: Centimetres and metres
outcomes: Learner can measure in cm and m, convert between them and estimate lengths
misconceptions: Believes 1 m = 10 cm
Starts measuring from the edge of the ruler instead of the 0 mark
hooks: Measure a cricket bat and the pitch length

topics.title: Distance around a shape
outcomes: Learner can find the length of the boundary of simple shapes
misconceptions: Adds only two sides of a rectangle to find the boundary
hooks: How much lace for the edge of a tablecloth?

topics.title: Adding and subtracting larger numbers
outcomes: Learner can add and subtract 3- and 4-digit numbers in shopping and travel situations
misconceptions: Misaligns digits when numbers have different lengths
hooks: Daisy and Lou’s trip to Mawlynnong, Meghalaya

topics.title: Estimating costs
outcomes: Learner can estimate a total cost before calculating and check if the answer is reasonable
misconceptions: Thinks the estimate and exact answer must be the same
hooks: Will ₹500 be enough for the trip shopping list?

topics.title: Grams and kilograms
outcomes: Learner can measure and compare weights in g and kg and convert
misconceptions: Believes 1 kg = 100 g
hooks: Packets of 200 g biscuits and 1 kg sugar

topics.title: Millilitres and litres
outcomes: Learner can measure and compare capacities in ml and l
misconceptions: Thinks a 500 ml bottle holds more than a 1 l bottle because 500 > 1
hooks: How many 200 ml glasses in a 1 l jug of nimbu-pani?

topics.title: Multiplication facts and patterns
outcomes: Learner can use multiplication facts up to 10 × 10 and spot patterns in a multiplication chart
misconceptions: Believes 6 × 0 = 6
hooks: Eggs in trays of 6

topics.title: Division as equal grouping and sharing
outcomes: Learner can solve division problems by grouping and sharing and link division to multiplication
misconceptions: Thinks division always gives a whole number with nothing left over
hooks: Packing 48 ladoos in boxes of 6

topics.title: Addition chart and strategies
outcomes: Learner can use patterns in an addition chart and mental strategies to add and subtract
misconceptions: Thinks adding the same number to both numbers changes the difference
hooks: NIM game: reach 10 first by adding 1 or 2

topics.title: Comparing counts in real data
outcomes: Learner can compare and find differences between large counts in tables
misconceptions: Subtracts in the wrong order when asked "how many more"
hooks: Tiger census numbers across Indian states

topics.title: Lines of symmetry
outcomes: Learner can find one or more lines of symmetry in shapes and letters
misconceptions: Believes every shape has exactly one line of symmetry
hooks: Fold a paper to make a symmetrical toran

topics.title: Completing symmetrical figures
outcomes: Learner can complete the other half of a figure to make it symmetrical
misconceptions: Copies the half without flipping it
hooks: Complete half of a rangoli

topics.title: Time to 5 minutes and a.m./p.m.
outcomes: Learner can read time to the nearest 5 minutes and use a.m. and p.m.
misconceptions: Thinks 12 noon is 12 a.m.
hooks: Train timings on a railway board

topics.title: Elapsed time and calendar
outcomes: Learner can find how long an activity takes and count days and weeks on a calendar
misconceptions: Adds minutes beyond 60 without converting to hours
hooks: How long is the Rajdhani journey?

topics.title: Multiplying by 10s and larger numbers
outcomes: Learner can multiply 2- and 3-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers and by 10
misconceptions: Multiplies only the ones digit (23 × 4 = 212)
hooks: Seats in 4 coaches of a train

topics.title: Dividing larger numbers
outcomes: Learner can divide 2- and 3-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers using sharing and repeated subtraction
misconceptions: Divides the larger digit by the smaller one regardless of position
hooks: Tickets shared among groups at the museum

topics.title: Tables and pictographs
outcomes: Learner can organise data in a table and read pictographs where one picture stands for many
misconceptions: Counts the pictures instead of using the key (1 picture = 5)
hooks: Rainfall in your town each month

topics.title: Simple bar graphs
outcomes: Learner can read simple bar graphs and answer comparison questions
misconceptions: Reads the width of bars as their value
hooks: Votes for class monitor
